gpaPolicyFacts.text: Assured admission combines diploma type with class rank and, outside the top quarter, test scores. Top-75% applicants without qualifying scores receive holistic review; fourth-quarter applicants need qualifying scores.

A cumulative unweighted high-school GPA of 3.25 is one guaranteed-admission route; UNT standardizes GPAs to a 4.0 scale. A separate 3.0 core-course GPA route uses four years each of English, math and science and three of social science. These are alternative eligibility routes, not a class-average comparison.

An unweighted 3.25 GPA on a 4.0 scale or top-quartile rank is a guaranteed-admission route; other class-rank routes combine test scores and advanced credits. Applicants outside these criteria receive individual holistic review.

For 2025–26 and 2026–27 terms, SFA is test optional and automatically admits applicants in the top quarter. Other applicants are reviewed using available information; some scholarships still require scores.

gpaPolicyFacts.text: OU gives greatest weight to high-school grades and reviews core GPA, course rigor and test scores. It compares a student's GPA with other OU applicants and applicants from the same high school; this does not publish a complete recalculation formula.

gpaPolicyFacts.text: OSU uses a weighted cumulative GPA based on a 4.0 scale for admissions and scholarships. Its published page does not specify individual course bonuses. A 3.0 GPA in the 15-unit core is one assured-admission route; programs can have additional criteria.

Admissions evaluates GPAs on a 4.0 base and gives one extra grade point only to AP, IB and clearly indicated dual-enrollment courses. GPAs containing Honors or Pre-AP weight may be recalculated. Subject eligibility and lower-grade treatment are not fully specified here; do not implement a complete formula from this statement.

gpaPolicyFacts.text: Assured admission requires the 16-unit curriculum and one performance criterion: 3.0 cumulative GPA, ACT 20, SAT 1040, or top-half rank. Engineering and other colleges may add requirements.

Assured admission uses a cumulative weighted or unweighted high-school GPA of 3.25, or ACT 21/SAT 1060; college coursework taken in high school must have at least a 2.0 GPA when applicable. Applicants below these criteria receive individual review; some majors have additional requirements.

profiles.name: University of Texas at El Paso

gpaPolicyFacts.text: UTEP offers assured-admission paths using diploma type, high-school rank and test scores, plus reviewed admission through the START Program for eligible students outside those paths. START provides first-term math and/or English preparation.

An unweighted GPA of 3.0 is one automatic-admission route, with or without test scores. Other routes include eligible rank, GPA/test combinations and at least 12 transferable dual-credit hours with a 2.5 GPA; required diploma plans and program criteria still apply.

profiles.name: McGill University
profiles.population: Applicants following a U.S. high-school curriculum

gpaPolicyFacts.text: McGill reviews grades 10–12, including program prerequisites and failed or repeated courses. Self-report grades in their original format, without averaging, converting or applying weight. Published typical admission grades vary by program and are not a university-wide GPA formula.
For Fall 2027, listed programs offer an ACT/SAT opt-out. Program-specific subject prerequisites remain; grades from an American high school do not map to McGill's undergraduate grading scale.

profiles.preparationScope: Senior/Grade 12 equivalent English only. Additional prerequisites vary by program; earlier English credits do not establish this requirement.

gpaPolicyFacts.text: Oxford's U.S. qualification routes use four AP exams at grade 5, or three APs at grade 5 plus ACT/SAT, with required AP subjects and score thresholds set by the course's A-level-equivalent standard. ACT/SAT thresholds span 31–33 and 1460–1480. These are qualification routes, not admitted-student middle-50% ranges.

Math-requiring courses prefer Calculus BC when available and accept AB if BC is unavailable. AB and BC do not count as two separate subjects. SAT/ACT scores must come from one sitting; Oxford does not superscore.
